title_guess: Monetary policy: price stability, liquid money and the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee

segments.teaches: many inputs drive economic growth; price stability (low, predictable inflation) is a key precondition for steady long-term growth

elements.what: maroon India silhouette
fan of black arrows converging on the map from the left
arrow from the map to a rising bar-chart icon labelled economic growth
balance-scales with goods in a yellow glowing circle labelled Price Stability
light-blue box under the circle: why price stability matters
definition text above the circle with a pointer line into it

segments.notes: The arrow fan is a quick 'many factors' device; one factor then pops in with a glow.

segments.teaches: RBI controls inflation to keep prices stable; inflation comes from demand, demand from purchasing power, purchasing power from money

elements.what: compact top row: price stability -> India -> economic growth
black muscular arms gripping the RBI emblem, with the word CONTROL across them
RBI emblem and letters
chain built right to left: Inflation (up-arrow to price stability) <- Demand <- Purchasing Power <- Money

segments.notes: Backward chaining: each new cause is added to the LEFT of the previous one, so the chain reads forward once complete.

segments.teaches: only part of money can be spent: blocked money (locked up, cannot be used quickly) does not create demand

elements.what: Money splits into Blocked Money and Liquid Money with green elbows
grey definition box under Blocked Money
house with trees labelled 5 crore and its owner
airplane labelled 25 lakh and a seller figure holding a 25 lakh tag
red crosses on the arrows between owner and airplane
dotted curved arrow from the Blocked Money box to the house

segments.notes: Running numeric example: rich on paper (5 crore house) but cannot buy a 25 lakh item. Background dims to light grey during the example to focus attention.

segments.teaches: liquid money (cash, demand deposits) drives purchasing power, demand and inflation; fixed deposits, PF and PPF are blocked

elements.what: stair-shaped light-blue band joining Liquid Money -> Purchasing Power -> Demand -> Inflation up to the price-stability row
yellow definition box under Liquid Money
square-bullet example lists under each money type (FD, PF, PPF / cash, demand deposits)

segments.notes: One continuous highlight band traces the causal path through the whole diagram.

segments.teaches: monetary policy is RBI's control over the supply of liquid money

elements.what: chain keeps only the liquid-money path; 'Supply of' added in handwriting font above Liquid Money
CONTROL arms with emblem move under Liquid Money
arch-shaped badge (tombstone outline) with MONETARY POLICY curved on top and 'Supply of Liquid Money' inside, standing on the CONTROL arms

segments.notes: Concept compression: the whole chain collapses into one reusable badge. Background turns grey.

segments.teaches: the Monetary Policy Committee has six members: three from RBI (Governor as chair, a Deputy Governor, one RBI official) and three nominated by the government

elements.what: dotted elbow arrows from the badge to the committee
six numbered person icons behind a table, one or two coloured red
dark plaque on the table: Monetary Policy Committee
government emblem with Ministry of Finance label
red [Chairman] tag over the RBI Governor label
thin arrows from role labels (Governor, Deputy Governor, RBI official) to individual members

segments.notes: Committee as a seated row of identical figures; colour singles out members.

segments.teaches: RBI uses qualitative tools (affect liquid money indirectly) and quantitative tools (affect it directly)

elements.what: monetary-policy badge in the centre
curved arrows from the badge top to Qualitative (left) and Quantitative (right)
grey explanation box on each side
dotted elbow arrows back into the Liquid Money band, labelled 'affects indirectly' and 'affects directly'

segments.notes: Symmetric two-sided layout around a central badge.

elements.what: next-video and playlist panels
app promo phone mock-up and app-store badges
